analyst_view.overall: Early view: Leverkusen want the ball and press high under Carles Martínez, but they had lost three of four competitive games before winning the derby in Köln and have conceded 17 league goals. Paderborn are unbeaten in four league games, sit compact in a 3-3-2-2 and have a goalkeeper in form in Nahuel Noll. Leverkusen also have Europa League football to manage around this round.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.6 goals. I lean higher: Leverkusen scored at least twice in each of their first ten competitive games under Martínez and their league games have produced 37 goals in nine, partly because their defence has been loose (four conceded at home to Stuttgart). Paderborn are hard to beat but scored twice against Frankfurt last time out.

corners.text: The site expects 11.4 corners, 8.2 for Leverkusen. That already reflects a possession side against a deep back five, and Leverkusen had almost 60% of the ball in Köln. Paderborn are not purely passive (they finished strongly with the ball at Gladbach), so I see no reason to move it.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.4 cards. I lean higher because Leverkusen's games have been card-heavy lately: eleven yellows in the derby and seven in the first hour against Stuttgart. Paderborn picked up three at Gladbach and coach Ralf Kettemann was booked against Frankfurt.

shots.text: The site has 31.8 shots, 21.6 of them Leverkusen's. Leverkusen took 15 in the derby and Paderborn's back five blocks a lot, so more than 20 for the hosts feels high, while Paderborn's 10.2 is generous for a side with eight league goals. I lean a little lower.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.3 on target. Leverkusen's finishers (Patrik Schick, Aleix García from free kicks) should test Noll often, and Paderborn hit the bar and scored twice against Frankfurt, so I stay close to the number.
